title: Investigate and remediate session-handoff pointer-drift causing GPU OOMs and KV-index corruption
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Multiple customer escalations across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private environments reported sudden GPU OOM waves accompanied by KV-index inconsistencies and increasing memory fragmentation. Investigation points to a race during session handoff/eviction that leaves stale KV index pointers and unreclaimed heap 'shingles', which under sustained multi-tenant pressure causes allocator starvation for pinned GPU buffers and triggers OOMs.

Impact: High. Affected production tenants on both Hosted and Dedicated clusters (two enterprise customers on Dedicated reported 10-30% request failures during peak), one Private customer reported service degradation after a large model rollout. Incidents reproduced in staging under synthetic multi-session churn.

What we observed:
- Rapid increase in failed GPU allocations concurrent with high session churn.
- Heap fragmentation metrics showed many small free segments and growing external fragmentation ratio.
- KV index tombstone counts rose without corresponding compaction runs.
- Traces show session handoff path (SessionManager.transfer_session) performing non-atomic pointer updates during concurrent eviction paths.

Root cause (summary):
A three-part interaction: (1) a non-atomic session handoff sequence leaves transient stale references in the KV index when a session is rebalanced, (2) the runtime's slab allocator fails to coalesce adjacent small free regions due to a race with the KV-compactor thread, producing 'shingles' (fragmented free holes), and (3) GPU pinned allocations require contiguous pinned memory and fail early when fragmentation crosses a threshold. Under load this escalates to OOMs and occasionally to KV index corruption when tombstone cleanup runs into stale pointers.

Work done so far:
- Reproduced failure in multi-tenant staging harness (stories/run-oom-frag-harness).
- Added heavy instrumentation: session handoff traces, per-segment free-list sizes, compaction lock contention counters, and GPU-pinned allocation failure histograms.
- Built and deployed a safety hotpatch (PR #8342) that: (a) places an atomic handoff fence in SessionManager.transfer_session, (b) adds reference-count guard for session objects during eviction, and (c) adds a temporary allocator coalescing pass that runs during low-traffic windows to reduce fragmentation.
- Hotpatch can be toggled via runtime flag runtime.flags.session_handoff_safety and runtime.flags.alloc_coalesce_emergency.

Current status and rollout:
- Hotpatch PR #8342 merged to release candidate branch on 2026-03-06.
- Canary rollout: Hosted clusters 3/6-3/8 (controlled rate) -> Dedicated pool A 3/9 -> Dedicated pool B + Private customer opt-in 3/11.
- Observed drop in GPU OOM rate by ~78% on canary nodes; KV tombstone deltas normalized.
- Continuing controlled rollout to remaining Dedicated nodes; full rollout planned by 2026-03-18 pending verification.

Immediate mitigations for impacted customers:
- Temporarily increased eviction aggressiveness (evict threshold lowered) to free pinned pages during surge windows.
- For Dedicated/Private customers, ops performed rolling worker restarts on affected pools to forcibly compact heap and drop transient stale pointers.

Open work / next steps:
- Production-quality fix: make handoff atomic in upstream SessionManager with formal invariants and unit tests (PR #8459 in progress).
- Replace emergency coalescer with deterministic allocation coalescer inside the allocator and add a fragmentation-aware placement policy for pinned allocations.
- Add end-to-end fuzz/chaos test in CI that reproduces session churn + model warmup scenarios.
- Add dashboard panels: free-segment-size distribution, compaction-failures, session-handoff-latency, and pinned-allocation-failure-rate.
- Postmortem writeup and customer-facing RCA to be prepared after rollout completes.

References & artifacts:
- Staging reproduction harness: gitlab.com/redwood/runtime/oom-frag-harness (internal)
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8342
- Follow-up PR (handoff atomic): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8459 (draft)
